clue.text: Film a vessel on a river

blocks.note: taken as written
a vat is a large vessel for liquids
a river: A for a, R the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A scene for a movie: a boat floating on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the river after the vessel, as in a down-reading charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Avatar is James Cameron's 2009 blockbuster movie, so the title answers a one-word film clue.

blocks.note: AC is the abbreviation for aircraftman, the lowest RAF rank
quaint means attractively, noticeably old-fashioned

explanation.surface: Someone briefs an RAF aircraftman whose manner seems charmingly dated.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquaint someone with a fact is to make them aware of it, a close synonym of telling them.

clue.text: Raging at fame, or fat cats, in reality

indicators.note: something raging is wild and out of control, so the letters that follow are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: fifteen letters taken as written, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: Someone fumes at the celebrity and wealth of overpaid bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are adverbial ways of saying 'actually', introducing what is truly the case.

clue.text: Appeared in play - lengthy? Not half!

indicators.note: not half tells us to throw away half of the word, keeping only the other half

blocks.note: protracted means drawn out, lengthy

explanation.surface: A question about whether a stage role was long, answered with the slangy 'Not half!' meaning 'Very!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'absolutely', but here it drops the first five of PROTRACTED's ten letters to leave ACTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear in a play is to perform a role on stage, which is what an actor who acted did.

clue.text: English writer, Eliot, is wandering around lake

indicators.note: wandering things stray from their path, so these letters move out of their order
around says the rearranged letters wrap themselves about another piece

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: One English author, Eliot, rambles round a lake like a Romantic poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliot looks like the writer being defined, but that name is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Sillitoe was an English novelist, author of Saturday Night and Sunday Morning.

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
an order is a rule or command

explanation.surface: A question on Irish politics: is Home Rule the right thing?
explanation.definitionFit: Something in order is proper or fitting for the situation, as when a remark is in order.

blocks.note: first meaning: the royal dynasty that fought York in the Wars of the Roses
second meaning: the historic administrative centre of Lancashire

explanation.surface: A dwelling located in a provincial town.
explanation.walkthrough: A county town is the administrative capital of an English county; House with a capital H is a royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Lancaster was an English royal dynasty, and Lancaster is the traditional county town of Lancashire.

indicators.note: an eccentric is odd and off-centre, so the letters before it are set in an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: A description of a quiet, odd character who is into horse racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like an abbreviation for R, but all five letters are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse racing has long been nicknamed the sport of kings because of its royal patronage.

clue.text: Trees cut across area used for festival

indicators.note: trees that are cut are chopped up, so their letters are broken and rearranged
across means lying over and around another piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Felled trees cleared from a piece of land to make room for a fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival celebrating the resurrection, held in spring.

indicators.note: something cast in metal is set inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a ring is a call on the telephone, a bell

explanation.surface: A bell is struck after being forged in metal.
explanation.walkthrough: Bang reads as a noise to go with the bell, but it is the hairstyle: bangs is American for a fringe of hair cut across the forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: A bang is a fringe of hair cut straight across the forehead, the American term for the same style.

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other, here the lodgings wrapping round

blocks.note: quarters are living accommodation, lodgings
one who pounds, batters

explanation.surface: A brawler at a boarding house is laying into some fast food.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarter-pounders are hamburgers weighing a quarter of a pound before cooking, as sold by fast-food chains.

indicators.note: among puts the first word within the company of the others, so it is placed inside them

blocks.note: taken as written
a band is a group, especially of musicians
done in means exhausted, worn out

explanation.surface: Worn-out members of a party left stranded on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone marooned has been left behind and deserted somewhere, which is to be abandoned.

clue.text: Enough taste without pinch of salt

indicators.note: a pinch is a tiny amount, so only the opening letter of the next word is taken
without means lacking, so the small piece is removed from the word before

blocks.note: to sample is to taste, or a sample is a taste
the opening letter of salt

explanation.surface: Cooking advice: the dish tastes fine without adding seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking something with a pinch of salt means doubting it; here the phrase is purely mechanical.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means more than sufficient, plenty, so it stands for enough.

indicators.note: heading means going on top or in front, so the first piece leads the second

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
a table is a chart of figures

explanation.surface: A record topping the music charts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notable is remarkable and worthy of attention, as something striking is.

clue.text: Blunder by individual turning up hidden bomb, perhaps

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side
in a down clue turning up means reading the word from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a boob is a silly mistake
a party is a person, as in the guilty party or a party to a contract

explanation.surface: Someone's mistake leads to a concealed explosive being discovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a piece to keep, but it only sets the blunder beside the turned individual; a party is a person in legal or jokey usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A booby trap is a disguised device set to go off when touched, of which a concealed bomb is one example.

blocks.note: first meaning: leave one's job at the end of a career
second meaning: withdraw or fall back, as an army does

explanation.surface: Someone downs tools while on a quiet getaway.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is both to give up employment for good and to withdraw from a place or position.

blocks.note: first meaning: a boiled candy shaped like a pear
second meaning: a pear-shaped hanging jewel, as on an earring

explanation.walkthrough: Sweet looks like an adjective describing the jewellery, but in Britain a sweet is a candy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear drop is a British boiled sweet and also a pear-shaped jewel worn hanging from an earring or necklace.

clue.text: Husband leaving nurse in leafy glade

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter departs from the word

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
to harbour a feeling is to nurse it

explanation.surface: A husband walks out on a nurse in a woodland clearing.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbour is a shady garden shelter or bower formed by trees or climbing plants.

clue.text: Brief plan to promote actress (Rosalind or Jane)

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a ruse is a crafty plan or trick
to sell an idea is to promote it

explanation.surface: A short strategy to boost an actress's career, with two candidates named.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosalind Russell and Jane Russell were both Hollywood film actresses, sharing this surname.

clue.text: Miser, for example, returned, after wages, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is caught by ear, so take its sound and not its spelling
something returned comes back the other way, so the letters run backwards
after tells us the turned piece is placed behind the other

blocks.note: screw is old British slang for wages
e.g. is the abbreviation for for example

explanation.surface: A tightfisted employer comes back to the subject of pay.
explanation.walkthrough: SCROO is just the first syllable of the name said aloud, sounding like screw, slang for a wage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer Scrooge, Dickens's tight-fisted character, has become a byword for any mean person.

indicators.note: reportedly means as told by word of mouth, so the next word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a dressing is a sauce for salad

explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the answer and SAUCE sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A well is a spring of water, the place where a supply of water originates, a source.

clue.text: Manipulated SP, once, as a gamble

indicators.note: manipulated means handled and worked around, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A betting cheat once fiddled the starting price to win a wager.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is the betting term for starting price, the odds when a race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on spec means doing it speculatively, on the chance that it pays off, a risk.

clue.text: Independent broadsheet in New York, particularly good

indicators.note: in places the first two pieces inside the city abbreviation

blocks.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York
I is the abbreviation for independent
the FT, or Financial Times, is a British broadsheet newspaper

explanation.surface: British newspapers on sale in New York are of high quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The Independent is a real British paper too, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Nifty is informal for skilful or neat, describing something especially effective or clever.

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: to read a subject at university is to study it
a poker stirs up, raises, a fire

explanation.surface: Someone almost reads up on an arsonist's methods.
explanation.walkthrough: A fire-raiser is usually an arsonist; here it is the iron rod that livens up a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Stud poker is a card game in which some of each player's cards are dealt face up.

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across suntrap, hot and obviously

explanation.surface: A holiday snapshot taken in a sunny spot, clearly a scorcher.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the last letter of suntrap and ends at the first of obviously.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is a casual photograph, short for snapshot.

blocks.note: a prairie is a vast grassy plain
a schooner is a tall glass for sherry or beer

explanation.surface: A clear pane fitted in a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: Plain glass reads as one thing, clear glass; the two words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie schooner was the covered wagon used by American pioneers crossing the plains.

indicators.note: inside puts the first pieces within the last one

blocks.note: a school of thought or followers, a cult
taken as written
to tap a phone is to monitor it

explanation.surface: A pupil, a class monitor, fires a slingshot in class.
explanation.walkthrough: Monitor suggests a prefect at school, but it is the verb for eavesdropping on a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Catapult is the British word for a slingshot, so both name the same Y-shaped weapon; as a verb, to catapult is to sling.

clue.text: Scandalmonger, first to get very large drink

indicators.note: first to marks taking only the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the opening letter of get
OS stands for outsize, a clothing label meaning very large
a sip is a small drink

explanation.surface: A rumour-monger is first to get an extra-large drink at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip is a person who spreads rumours about others, someone who peddles scandal.
